llm.reply:
The genes associated with cystic fibrosis include NCBIGene:1080, name: CF transmembrane conductance regulator [1]. Another associated gene is NCBIGene:2212, name: Fc gamma receptor IIa [3]. The answer also includes NCBIGene:7040, name: transforming growth factor beta 1 [4].

## Clinical features

Bronchiectasis is a listed clinical feature [15]. Hemoptysis is a listed clinical feature [28]. Clubbing of fingers is also a listed clinical feature [19].

## Liver disease context

Liver disease affects a substantial proportion of patients with cystic fibrosis, but encephalopathy is a rare complication [26: "Cystic fibrosis liver disease (CFLD) affects a large proportion of cystic fibrosis (CF) patients; however encephalopathy is a rare complication"]. Classical hepatic encephalopathy can occur in end-stage liver disease [26: "classical hepatic encephalopathy can be a feature of end-stage liver disease"]. Hyperammonemic encephalopathy can be triggered in previously stable cystic fibrosis liver disease, including by systemic corticosteroids [26: "\"hyperammonemic encephalopathy\" can be precipitated in previously stable CFLD by various triggers including systemic corticosteroids"].

An associated gene is NCBIGene:1080, CF transmembrane conductance regulator [1]. Another associated gene is NCBIGene:2212, Fc gamma receptor IIa [3]. A further associated gene is NCBIGene:7040, transforming growth factor beta 1 [4].

## Disease and features

The disease name is Cystic fibrosis [2]. The MedGen title is Cystic fibrosis [6]. The literature entity name is Cystic Fibrosis [7]. Listed clinical features include Asthma [11]. Another is Hepatosplenomegaly [30].
